subject: Integration sprint, evaluation criteria & immediate next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@olivetech.com>, James Park <james@olivetech.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-19T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Integration sprint, evaluation criteria & immediate next steps

Hi Emma / James —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before engineering work begins.

1) Success criteria (what OliveTech will use to accept the POC)
- 95% intent-matching on the 2k sample utterances you provided (F1 >= 0.95)
- End-to-end 99th percentile latency < 350ms for chat flows <= 200 tokens
- Embedding similarity retrieval (top-3 recall) >= 92% on your benchmark set
- No PII leakage; audit logs enabled for every request during the trial

2) Technical integration overview (high level)
- Primary integration: Redwood REST SDK for streaming chat (server-side SDK)
- Fallback: HTTP chunked streaming to /v1/generate when WebSockets unavailable
- Tool calling: use JSON-schema tool payloads; we'll provide a tools manifest and sample handler
- Authentication: API key; for Dedicated/Private we can enable mTLS and VPC controls

3) Ownership & roles
- OliveTech: Emma (product lead) — success criteria sign-off; James (platform) — infra + token provisioning
- Redwood: Sean — commercial lead; Dev — implementation lead; Monica — CS owner for acceptance

4) Proposed timeline
- 11/20: kick-off tech scoping call (30m) — Dev + James
- 11/24: SDK integration completed (internal smoke tests)
- 11/27: End-to-end validation with benchmark dataset
- 11/30: Review results; acceptance decision

5) Immediate asks from OliveTech
- Provide the 2k sample utterances and embedding benchmark (CSV or JSONL)
- Confirm preferred auth (API key vs. SSO/mTLS)
- Any procurement timeline constraints (procurement@olivetech.com)

I've attached a first-pass evaluation spreadsheet and a machine-readable integration matrix (CSV) to map our SDK routes to your handlers.

Attachments: olivetech-eval-success-criteria.xlsx, redwood-integration-matrix-v1.csv

If this looks good I'll schedule the 11/20 tech scoping with Dev + James. Seen? Reply with any redlines.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Thanks — quick technical checklist ahead of today's scoping call:

- Required endpoints (examples)
  - POST /v1/chat/stream  (streaming SSE or WebSocket)
  - POST /v1/generate     (chunked HTTP streaming fallback)
  - POST /v1/embeddings   (batch embeddings)
  - POST /v1/tools/invoke (tool-calling proxy)

- Auth
  - We will generate a scoped API key for the POC. For Dedicated customers we can enable mTLS; let us know if you need that now.

- Streaming details
  - Preferred: WebSocket for low-latency conversational streams; we'll provide a minimal client example in the SDK (node/python).
  - Fallback: chunked transfer encoding with "data: " SSE frames.

- Tool calling
  - Send tool manifest JSON; our runtime will return a "tool_call" structure. We'll provide a sample handler: POST /internal/tools/handle -> returns {status, output}

- Metrics to capture in your environment
  - per-request latency, token counts, model variant, response completeness flag, and any tool-call durations.

Sample cURL for embeddings (for quick smoke tests):

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-embed-1","input":["sample utterance 1","sample utterance 2"]}'

I'll drop the sample SDK snippets to the Drive link after the call; James, if you can confirm whether you prefer WebSocket or HTTP fallback for the first pass that will help us prioritize.

—Dev
